case_name: Chahat Khan v State of Haryana
respondent:
State of Haryana
Supreme Court of India

9 March 1972
Cr.A. No. 72 of 1970 (Arising as an appeal by Special Leave from the Judgment and Order Dt. 24 September 1969 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Cr. A. No. 174 of 1969).
The Judgment was delivered by: GROVER, J.
1.  This is an appeal by Special Leave from the Judgment of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.
2.  Chahat Khan, Bhup Singh, Harun and Mohar all of whom belong to Keri Nuh, were tried under Section 302, read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 by the Additional Sessions Judge, Gurgaon for the murder of Ahmad Khan on the Morning of the 4th July1968. facts: Chahat Khan, Bhup Singh, Harun and Mohar were tried under Section 302, read with S.34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 by the Additional Sessions Judge, Gurgaon for the murder of Ahmad Khan on the Morning of the 4th July1968.
The learned Additional Sessions Judge found that the prosecution case had been established and that these persons were guilty of the offences with which they had been charged.
They were sentenced to imprisonment for life and a fine of Rs.200/- and in default of payment of fine they were directed to undergo further imprisonment for six months.
issues: Whether the prosecution had failed to prove that there was any motive on the part of the appellants to inflict injuries on the deceased.
Whether the intention was only to cause him a hurt or the most a grievous hurt, rather than to commit murder.
petitioner_arguments: According to the prosecution evidence injury No.1 which caused the death of Ahmad Khan could not be attributed to the appellant.
The witnesses are not very clear whether it was the appellant or Bhup Singh who had caused injury No.1.
The gun was hanging in his shoulders and he only used his lathi, showing that he had no intention to kill the deceased.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution examined a number of eye-witnesses, namely, Nazar Khan, P.W.2, Deena, P.W.3, Chatru, P.W.4, P.W.6 and Hussain Khan, P.W.7.
These witnesses supported the prosecution version and their evidence was accepted by the learned Additional Sessions Judge.
The injury on the head which resulted in the death of Ahmad Khan had been caused by Chahat Khan.
court_reasoning: Injury No.1, a lacerated wound, found on the head of the deceased, which resulted in fracture of the left parietal bone, according to the ocular evidence, was inflicted by Chahat Khan.
He had clearly exceeded the common intention and was thus guilty of murder under clause Thirdly of S.300 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
holding: We find no merit in this appeal and it is dismissed.
